questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

Saying this, she (1)/ storm out of the room, (2)/ leaving her bags behind. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Reading this sentence we understand that the above-mentioned sentence talked about past activities that completed at a particular time.
 
• Thus we use **stormed ou**t__ instead of** storm out.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** **

 
• If any sentence gives the sense of completion of any activity we should be use past tense.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.** 

We recommend that (1)/ you keep your (2)/ advice to yourself. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (4)** i.e. **"No error".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Two clauses are connected by 'that'.
 
• "We recommend" here 'We' is the plural subject and 'recommend' is the plural verb. It is in the simple present tense.
 
• "you keep your advice to yourself" Here the subject is 'you'. 'keep' is the verb. It is also in the simple present tense.
 
• 'your' is used here as a possessive adjective. 'advice' is used here as a noun. 'yourself' is the reflexive pronoun.
 
• All the parts of speech and verbs are used correctly.
 
• Hence the sentence is grammatically and contextually correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is "No error".** **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****'Advise'** is a verb.** 'Advice'** is an uncountable noun.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.** 

The CM ﬂew ______ the ﬂooded areas in a helicopter.
questions.solution:
Helicopter flies in the air i.e it can only fly above** **or ***over** *the flooded areas.

Hence, **option 2* ***is the correct answer.

__Correct sentence:__*The CM ﬂew **over **the ﬂooded areas in a helicopter. *

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.** 

Her mother is anxious _____ her health.
questions.solution: Anxious = worried. And one can only be worried **about **something. Hence, Option 1) *About *is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.** 

Primitive
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3)** i.e.** 'Basic'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primitive: (आदिम)** - Being the first or earliest of the kind or existing in a simple or basic form.

 
 
• **Example:** The tribe lived in a primitive society with no written language.
 
 
 
• **Basic: (मूल)** - Forming an essential foundation or starting point; fundamental.
 
 
• **Example:** Understanding basic math is essential for advanced studies.
 
 
 
• From the above explanation, it is clear that Basic is similar to Primitive in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Basic'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present: (वर्तमान)** - Existing or happening now.

 
 
• **Example:** In the present era, technology plays a vital role in our lives.
 
 
 
• **New: (नया)** - Not existing before; made, introduced, or discovered recently or now for the first time.
 
 
• **Example:** They moved to a new city for better opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Modern: (आधुनिक)** - Relating to the present or recent times as opposed to the remote past.
 
 
• **Example:** He prefers modern architecture over traditional styles.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.** 

Deﬁnite
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Complete.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Definite"** means something that is clearly stated or decided; not vague or doubtful. (स्पष्ट या निश्चित)
 
 
• **Example: **She gave me a definite answer to my question.
 
 
 
• **"Complete" **refers to something that is entire or full; having all the necessary parts. (पूर्ण)
 
 
• **Example: **After months of hard work, the project is now complete.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Complete.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Inexact **(असटीक): Not precise or accurate.
 
 
• **Example:** His measurements were inexact, which led to errors in the construction.
 
 
 
• **Unclear **(अस्पष्ट): Not easy to see, hear, or understand.
 
 
• **Example: **The instructions were unclear, causing confusion among the participants.
 
 
 
• **Vague** (अस्पष्ट): Not clearly expressed, known, described, or decided.
 
 
• **Example:** She gave a vague description of the suspect, making it difficult for the police to identify him.

questions.question:

Condemn
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Criticize**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.** 

Virtual
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Virtual"** means something that is almost or nearly as described, but not completely or according to strict definition. (वास्तविकता में नहीं)
 
 
• **Example:** In the virtual world of online gaming, players can become anyone they want to be.
 
 
 
• **"Authentic"** refers to something that is genuine and real, not false or copied; it is the opposite of virtual. (प्रामाणिक)
 
 
• **Example:** The museum displayed an authentic piece of ancient pottery.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Virtual'** is **'Authentic'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Fundamental** (मूलभूत): Serving as an essential component.
 
 
• **Example:** Understanding the fundamentals of mathematics is crucial for advanced studies.
 
 
 
• **Implied** (निहित): Suggested without being directly expressed.
 
 
• **Example:** Her silence implied consent.
 
 
 
• **Indirect** (अप्रत्यक्ष): Not directly caused by or resulting from something.
 
 
• **Example:** The statement was an indirect way of criticizing his work.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.** 

Now and again
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Occasionally**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Now and again"** means something that happens occasionally or from time to time. (कभी-कभी)

 
 
• **Example:** Now and again, she likes to take a walk in the park to clear her mind.
 
 
 
• **"Occasionally"** refers to something that happens infrequently or at irregular intervals. (कभी-कभी)
 
 
• **Example:** I only see my cousins occasionally, usually during holidays.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Occasionally**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Always** (हमेशा): At all times; on all occasions.

 
 
• **Example:** She always takes her coffee with sugar.
 
 
 
• **To be continued** (जारी रहेगा): Something that will be continued at a later time.
 
 
• **Example:** The story was left on a cliffhanger, to be continued in the next episode.
 
 
 
• **At present time or future** (वर्तमान समय या भविष्य में): Refers to something happening now or in the future.
 
 
• **Example:** We are currently working on the project, and it will be completed in the near future.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.** 

Heavy metals

P: in many applications

Q: are today being

R: replaced by polymers
questions.solution:
It is clear that Q is first in sequence since it utilizes *are today being*. Rule out 1) and 3).

QRP: Heavy metals are today being replaced by polymers in many applications.

QPR: Heavy metals are today being in many applications replaced by polymers.

Clearly, Option 2) *QRP *is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.** 

One should

P: think calmly

Q: and clearly

R: learn how to
questions.solution:
*Clearly *requires a verb to be linked with it. It is evident from this that Q will immediately follow P (*think*). Rule out 2) and 3*). *A sentence can't end with **to** => rule out 1). Hence, Option 4) *RPQ *is the correct answer.

One should learn how to think calmly and clearly.
